evidenceContract.rule: A candidate success string is never sufficient. Capture the specified fixture, application, or process postcondition for every successful trial.
evidenceContract.eventEndpoint: GET /events returns the browser fixture event ledger; POST or GET /reset clears it.

rows.name: Local browser DOM fixture
rows.precondition: Start event-server.mjs, open /dom-fixture.html in an ordinary local browser window, then GET /reset and confirm an empty event ledger.
rows.action: Target the browser window and click Click target, type a unique token into Text target, drag at least 15 CSS pixels in Drag target, and scroll Scroll target.
rows.postcondition: The DOM page visibly says each action was recorded, the typed token and non-zero scroll position are visible, and GET /events contains corresponding click, type, drag, and scroll events with isTrusted: true.
rows.reset: GET /reset, reload /dom-fixture.html, clear Text target, and return Scroll target to scrollTop 0.

rows.name: Local browser canvas fixture
rows.precondition: Start event-server.mjs, open /canvas-fixture.html, focus the labelled canvas, then GET /reset and confirm an empty event ledger.
rows.action: Click a labelled grid coordinate, drag across the grid, scroll its wheel, and hold two keyboard keys simultaneously before releasing them.
rows.postcondition: GET /events has trusted pointer, scroll, key-down, and key-up events; each has canvas CSS/backing dimensions, DPR, coordinate fields, and heldKeys/heldButtons that show the simultaneous held state. The red canvas marker visibly moves.
rows.reset: GET /reset, reload /canvas-fixture.html, and release all candidate-held input before the next trial.

rows.name: Ordinary logged-in browser profile
rows.precondition: An ordinary user browser profile is already running and has a visible profile-backed state such as history, cookies, autofill, or an authenticated session.
rows.action: Rediscover or target its existing window and navigate through visible browser UI without launching a replacement automation profile.
rows.postcondition: A visible browser page and browser UI confirm the original profile remains in use, including one observable pre-existing profile-backed state.
rows.reset: Return to the original tab or a new tab without clearing profile data; document the exact non-destructive restoration.
rows.trialNote: This profile-preservation check is intentionally not resettable without changing user state.

rows.name: VS Code/pie sidebar observation and navigation
rows.precondition: A VS Code window with pie available is visible and not minimized.
rows.action: Observe the sidebar, open pie if needed through visible UI, then navigate one representative sidebar state.
rows.postcondition: A screenshot or semantic observation shows the intended sidebar state and an observable selected/navigated control.
rows.reset: Return the sidebar to its initial visible state through the same UI.

rows.name: Native Win32 application
rows.precondition: A standard non-elevated Win32 application such as Notepad is launched with an empty disposable document.
rows.action: Discover the window, focus it, type a unique token, select it, and perform a visible pointer action.
rows.postcondition: The document visibly contains the exact token and the window remains the selected target after the pointer action.
rows.reset: Discard the unsaved disposable document and relaunch or clear it.

rows.name: Modern Windows application
rows.precondition: A non-elevated modern Windows application with a reversible visible control is available.
rows.action: Discover the window, focus it, and toggle or navigate one reversible visible control.
rows.postcondition: A screenshot or app state visibly confirms the intended control changed.
rows.reset: Return the reversible control to its original state.

rows.name: Godot editor selection, inspector interaction, and object drag
rows.precondition: Open godot-input-fixture in the installed Godot 4.7.1 editor; use the disposable DraggableProbe child in an ignored copy of the fixture.
rows.action: Select the object, alter one reversible inspector value, and drag the object in the editor viewport.
rows.postcondition: The editor visibly shows the intended selection, changed inspector value, and moved object.
rows.reset: Undo the inspector and viewport changes or reopen the disposable scene.

rows.name: Launched Godot fixture held and timed input
rows.precondition: Launch godot-input-fixture with the installed Godot 4.7.1 editor or executable and capture its stdout.
rows.action: Focus the running fixture and execute a timed sequence containing held movement keys, simultaneous keys, pointer drag, and wheel input.
rows.postcondition: The visible event log and stdout lines prefixed __EVENT__ show the expected ordered events and held_keys/held_buttons state, including simultaneous keys.
rows.reset: Use Reset visible event state, release all input, and relaunch the fixture if focus or state cannot be restored.

rows.name: Multi-window rediscovery
rows.precondition: Two or more distinguishable windows are open, including the local browser fixture and a disposable native application.
rows.action: Target each window in turn, alter its reversible visible state, then rediscover the first after foreground focus changes.
rows.postcondition: Each visible state change appears in its intended window and rediscovery identifies the first window rather than the most recently focused one.
rows.reset: Restore each reversible state and leave the fixture browser foregrounded.

rows.name: Cancellation during held key or mouse action
rows.precondition: Canvas fixture is focused and GET /reset confirms no prior event; the candidate supports cancellation of an in-flight held-input action.
rows.action: Start an action or sequence that holds a key and mouse button, then cancel while both are held.
rows.postcondition: Canvas state and GET /events show a release or cleared held state; a subsequent normal input succeeds without a stuck key/button.
rows.reset: Explicitly release all input, GET /reset, reload the canvas fixture if needed, and verify the held state is empty.

rows.name: Child-process termination and restart
rows.precondition: The candidate uses a separately identifiable native child process or equivalent runtime process and the DOM fixture server is available.
rows.action: Terminate the candidate runtime process during a non-destructive fixture session, then restart/reopen it and rediscover the fixture target.
rows.postcondition: The controlling evaluation process remains alive; restart is explicit and the fixture can receive and report one new trusted action after recovery.
rows.reset: Close the replacement runtime cleanly, GET /reset, and restore the fixture browser page.
rows.trialNote: Destructive lifecycle check; one successful recovery proof is sufficient.

rows.name: Multi-monitor mixed-DPI coordinates
rows.blockedReason: Blocked on this machine: no mixed-DPI multi-monitor arrangement is currently available. Do not infer a pass from single-monitor or same-DPI results.
rows.precondition: Two available monitors have different effective DPI scales, with a browser canvas fixture visible on each monitor in turn.
rows.action: Observe each fixture window and click the same labelled canvas CSS-grid coordinate after moving the window between monitors.
rows.postcondition: Each fixture event reports the intended CSS coordinate within the documented tolerance and its reported DPR agrees with the visible monitor scale.
rows.reset: Return the window to its original monitor and GET /reset after each placement.
